text:
support_jordan: Received escalation from ACME. Customer says SSE stream returned a 429 mid-stream, then their client retried and they observed duplicate token consumption and a partial transcript. Billing shows two small token usages instead of one continuous session.
jamie_runtime: Ugh. Do we have the raw stream IDs or session IDs? 429 mid-stream can happen if quota check runs per-request.
support_jordan: Attached logs from customer (pseudonymized) — session_id=acme-2026-03-10-77, stream_conn=conn-42. They claim client reconnect used the same bearer token.
priya_billing: I can see two separate meter entries for that session_id around the same minute, both small: 120 tokens and 98 tokens. Looks like retries created new charge lines.
jamie_runtime: Could be our SSE gateway treating reconnect as a separate session if connection wasn't gracefully resumed. Does client send any resume token?
support_jordan: Customer says no resume token. They expected streaming to continue after client-side backoff/reconnect. Their client is a Node app using fetch ReadableStream. Repro snippet they provided: 
```js
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } });
for await (const chunk of res.body) { console.log(chunk.toString()); }
// on 'error' do reconnect immediately
```
support_jordan: They reported the new connection got a 200 then SSE events, but with partial/duplicated content near the rejoin boundary.
devon_eng: Any chance the client is reading the same prefix twice because of our caching layer? If we cached the last prefix and replay on reconnect, but billing counted both the original partial and the replay, that could explain double charge.
jamie_runtime: We do prefix-KV caching, but we should only charge for served tokens once per logical completion. However current accounting keys are per-connection-id which would create two ledger lines for two connections.
priya_billing: Right — ledger keys are connection-scoped for streaming. If we naively create a new entry on reconnect, invoice will show two entries. We need an idempotency key or resume token mapping to collapse charges.
olivia_devex: Customer client is not sending a resume token. Could we make server send a small resume-id in the last event so client can pass it back on reconnect? Minimal change: include `event: resume_id\ndata: <hex>` every N tokens.
jamie_runtime: Good idea. But we need to verify existing behavior: why did 429 occur mid-stream? Was it quota enforcement or transient rate limit?
support_bot: (automated) Incident check: no global quota spike. Per-tenant quota for acme shows brief spike hitting burst quota at 03:11:22 UTC.
jamie_runtime: So they hit burst limit -> 429. Client immediately reconnected and got new connection id. No resume. That lines up.
devon_eng: Repro steps from my side: ran a script that opens SSE stream, triggers a synthetic quota 429 by hammering other tokens, then reconnects. I can repro duplicate accounting locally. Reproducer below: 
```bash
# open stream 1
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?sess=acme-test" > /tmp/stream1.log &
# trigger 429 by sending rapid parallel requests using same tenant
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"spam"}' & done
# reconnect stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?sess=acme-test" > /tmp/stream2.log
```
jamie_runtime: Thanks, Devon — that helped. Logs show connection IDs conn-101 and conn-102, both mapped to the same logical session but treated separately by billing.
priya_billing: For mitigation: we can (A) issue a one-time credit to customer and (B) implement server-side mapping from resume_id (if provided) or from session cookie to a single ledger key.
support_jordan: Customer wants root cause and fix. They'd like a reproducible mitigation while we fix the platform.
olivia_devex: Short-term workaround for customers: instruct client to implement exponential backoff and include a custom header `X-Resume-Session: <session_id>` on reconnect. Server currently ignores it but we can advise support to reconcile those ledger lines manually if they include the header value in logs.
jamie_runtime: Medium-term: change accounting to use `logical_session_id` if present. Add server-generated resume tokens as suggested. Also make 429 response include `Retry-After` and `resume_id` if we plan to support resuming.
support_jordan: Proposed customer message draft: "We're investigating. As a workaround, please use exponential backoff and pass `X-Resume-Session`. We've issued a credit; our engineering team is tracking a fix to avoid double billing on reconnects." Thoughts?
priya_billing: Fine from billing side. I'll draft the credit amount after we confirm exact token counts.
devon_eng: I'll file runtime ticket: RUNTIME-4231 "streaming: collapse ledger entries on resume_id or session header" and attach reproducer logs.
jamie_runtime: Also add tests to simulate mid-stream 429 + reconnect and assert single ledger line.
support_jordan: Customer replied: appreciated, will try header workaround. Follow-up scheduled for tomorrow.
priya_billing: I reconciled their tenant ledger; filed provisional credit for 220 tokens.
jamie_runtime: Quick note — we should audit other cases: token rotation (client replaced token mid-stream) might also create duplicates. Add to ticket.
support_jordan: Closing loop in thread once runtime ticket has a PR. Marking P1 -> P2 since workaround exists. :white_check_mark:
jamie_runtime: Assigning to myself and devon to implement resume tokens and accounting fix. :eyes:
support_jordan: Thanks team. I'll update customer once we have PR/ETA. :thumbsup:
